card.occupation: Part-time sales assistant at a high-street bakery chain in Walthamstow, working Saturday mornings and one weekday shift, about 12 hours a week
card.education_detail: Finished secondary school in Šiauliai, Lithuania, then a two-year vocational college course in commerce and retail. Later did a short ESOL course at a London adult education centre and a food hygiene certificate through work.
card.household: Lives with her husband Darius, 44, an electrician who works for a small building maintenance firm, and their daughter Emilija, 12, in Year 8 at a local secondary. They rent a two-bedroom ground-floor flat in a converted terraced house.
card.cultural_background: Lithuanian, born and raised in Šiauliai. Moved to London in 2006 at 23, shortly after Lithuania joined the EU, and met Darius, also Lithuanian, through friends in East London. Raised Catholic. Goes to Mass at the Lithuanian church in Bethnal Green at Christmas, Easter and on some Sundays, more out of habit and family feeling than strong devotion. Speaks Lithuanian at home and English at work and with her daughter's school. Has settled status and still thinks of herself as Lithuanian living in London.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and steady behind the counter. Turns up on time, knows the regulars' orders, and doesn't make a fuss. Has worked at the same bakery for six years and turned down a supervisor role because she wanted to keep her hours short around school. Before Emilija was born she worked full-time in a supermarket and briefly cleaned offices. Sees the job as useful income and something to get her out of the house, not a career.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks a lot, to work and around Walthamstow Marshes on nice weekends with Darius. Watches the basketball with him when Lithuania plays in a big tournament, because that is what you do, but doesn't follow it otherwise.
card.arts_persona: Watches Lithuanian and British TV, mostly crime dramas, Bake Off and whatever reality show is on. Listens to the radio in the kitchen. Has no interest in galleries or theatre. Went to see a musical once for a friend's birthday and thought it was fine but expensive. Likes the songs she grew up with.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Šiauliai every summer for two or three weeks to stay with her mum and see her sister's family. Flies Ryanair from Stansted or Luton. Other than that, has done a week in Spain twice. Not interested in trying new places much when the money could go on visiting home.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most evenings: cepelinai on special occasions, cold beetroot soup in summer, chicken and potatoes, pasta when she's tired. Buys rye bread, curd cheese and sausages at the Eastern European shop on the high road and everything else at Lidl. Calls the evening meal dinner. Brings home leftover bread from work. Not keen on spicy food and sticks to what she knows.
hobbies_and_interests: Cooking Lithuanian dishes for family and friends
Watching crime dramas and baking shows
Walking on Walthamstow Marshes and in Epping Forest
Video calls with her mum and sister on Sunday afternoons
Looking after a few pots of herbs and tomatoes in the small back garden
Facebook groups for Lithuanians in London
skills: Budgeting a household on a tight income
Fluent Lithuanian, good conversational English, some Russian from school
Baking bread and cakes from family recipes
card.career_goals: Nothing ambitious. Wants to keep her shifts while Emilija is at school, and maybe add a few more hours once she's older to save for a deposit on a flat. Has vaguely thought about a teaching assistant course but hasn't looked into it properly.
card.voice: Clear, practical English with a noticeable Lithuanian accent, careful vowels and sometimes dropped articles ('I go to shop after'). Has picked up London phrasing from nearly twenty years here: 'yeah', 'to be honest', 'it's alright', 'I was knackered'. Uses 'erm' when searching for a word and sometimes says 'how you say...' before finding it. Medium pace. Answers directly and briefly, then stops. If there's a silence she waits politely for the next question rather than filling it, and might add 'that's it, really' or 'yeah, so'. Says 'sorry?' when she hasn't quite caught something.
card.typing: Quick and functional. Capitalises the start of sentences most of the time but not always. Often leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Minimal punctuation, usually just full stops or nothing at the end. Occasional small grammar slips with articles and tenses. Short answers, no emojis, sometimes 'ok' or 'no idea'.
card.with_strangers: Polite and a bit reserved at first, friendly once she knows what's expected. Not chatty or performative, she answers what she's asked. Slightly wary of anything that sounds like selling or official forms. Warms up when talking about her daughter, food or home.
small_things: The bakery gets really busy on Saturday mornings
Emilija's school wants them to buy another thing for some project
Prices at Lidl have gone up a lot
Her landlord takes ages to fix anything
The weather in London is always grey, but at least winter isn't as cold as Lithuania
Darius is working on a job in Stratford this week
She made cepelinai at the weekend and it took all afternoon
deeper_things: Her dad died in 2015 and she couldn't get a flight home in time, which she still thinks about
She worries about her mum living alone in Šiauliai and sometimes feels guilty for being far away
Brexit made her feel less welcome for a while, and applying for settled status was stressful
They have tried to save for a flat for years, and renting in London feels like it will never end
She sometimes wonders whether Emilija will feel more English than Lithuanian, and whether that matters
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam set slightly below eye level on a kitchen table, framing her from mid-chest up, a little off-centre to the left. Daylight from a window to her right lights that side of her face, while the other side is a bit shadowed and the picture is slightly grainy. Woman in her early forties with a fair complexion, light blue eyes and a few fine lines around them, giving a small polite closed-mouth smile. Ash-blonde shoulder-length hair pulled back into a low ponytail, with a few loose strands at the front. No glasses, small gold stud earrings, and a thin gold chain with a small cross. She wears a plain navy V-neck jumper. Behind her is a small kitchen with white wall cupboards, a kettle and a bread bin on the worktop, a fridge with a school timetable and a couple of magnets held on with clips, and a wall calendar with handwritten notes. A tea towel hangs on the oven door at the edge of the frame.
